quarterly_data.quarter: Giantec Semiconductor annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (annual report): revenue RMB 1,221,283,642.63, up 18.77%, a record; net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 363,576,041.92, up 25.25%; net profit excluding non-recurring items RMB 330,860,381.08, up 25.37%; gross margin 57.29% (up 2.48 points). Quarterly revenue: Q1 RMB 261,066,428.63, Q2 RMB 313,788,926.25, Q3 RMB 357,954,251.60, Q4 RMB 288,474,036.15; Q4 net profit attributable RMB 43,724,372.73. The company attributes the growth to fast-rising shipments of DDR5 SPD chips, automotive-grade EEPROMs and high-performance industrial EEPROMs, which offset weaker consumer-electronics demand for its traditional products.

quarterly_data.quarter: Giantec Semiconductor annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Products and volumes (annual report): memory chips (SPD / TS, EEPROM, NOR flash) revenue RMB 1,069,498,596.13 in 2025, up 20.71%, gross margin 62.31% (up 2.08 points); mixed-signal chips (camera-motor drivers) RMB 113,921,878.25, up 8.49%, gross margin 22.45%; NFC and other RMB 37,863,168.25, up 1.57%. Memory chips output 292,241.85 ten-thousand units (+21.45%), sales 272,387.64 ten-thousand units (+14.74%), year-end inventory 59,045.84 ten-thousand units (+48.09%). Overseas revenue RMB 653,678,987.16 (+16.85%, gross margin 78.70%), with overseas customers mainly in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Korea; direct sales RMB 593,771,558.62 (gross margin 80.03%) versus distribution RMB 627,512,084.01 (35.77%). Wafers were 67.54% of cost of sales and packaging and testing 29.49%.

quarterly_data.quarter: Giantec Semiconductor annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: DDR5 SPD in 2025 (annual report): DDR5 SPD and DDR4 SPD chips are the memory-module line's main revenue sources; DDR5 SPD sales volume and revenue grew rapidly in 2025 as DDR5 module penetration rose and server and PC demand grew, while DDR4 SPD volume and revenue fell with DDR4's shrinking share. The company says the global DDR5 SPD suppliers in 2025 were mainly Giantec (in cooperation with Montage Technology) and Renesas, and that LPCAMM2 modules, which may replace soldered LPDDR5X in thin laptops, need 1 SPD chip each whereas soldered LPDDR5X needs none.
quarterly_data.figure: 1 SPD chip per LPCAMM2 module; none for soldered LPDDR5X

quarterly_data.quarter: Giantec Semiconductor annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Other lines in 2025 (annual report): smartphone camera-module and LCD-panel EEPROM and e-cigarette NOR flash volumes fell markedly and the company cut average prices of its main consumer products at the start of 2025, so consumer memory revenue and profit declined; from Q4 2025, as global memory supply-demand reversed, some memory chip models' Q4 volume and revenue grew rapidly YoY. WLCSP EEPROMs reached large-scale use in leading brands' AI glasses. Automotive-grade NOR flash entered several leading global automotive Tier-1 suppliers. Open-loop camera-motor driver sales fell on weaker handset demand and price cuts, while several optical-image-stabilisation (OIS) driver chips went into commercial use in major smartphone makers' mid- to high-end models.

quarterly_data.signal: R&D (annual report): R&D investment RMB 207,814,539.80 in 2025, up 18.34%, 17.02% of revenue, all expensed; 200 R&D staff (178 a year earlier). quarterly_data.quarter: Giantec Semiconductor annual report: 2025 Annual Report (03-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Business plan (annual report, company plan): building on its DDR5 SPD position, the company has laid out VPD chips for next-generation eSSD and CXL modules to strengthen its memory-module companion-chip leadership; in automotive it aims to rank in the top two, or even first, in the global automotive-grade EEPROM market; in industrial markets it will put more resources into high-performance products for new energy, industrial power and control, AIDC (AI data-center) power and solid-state transformers (SST); and it plans to develop new memory solutions in response to customers' long-term needs.
